title: Schema evolution ships as numbered forward-only migration files under a wrangler-managed directory
asA: operator who needs deploys reproducible from a git ref with no schema state outside version control
iWant: every schema change to be a new numbered `.sql` file under the wrangler-configured migrations directory, applied by the wrangler CLI
soThat: the schema shape at any deployed version can be read from the committed files and the vendor's own tooling is the single applier

acceptanceCriteria.description: The migrations directory named on the D1 binding (`migrations_dir` in the project's wrangler config; default `migrations/`) exists in the source tree and contains one `.sql` file per shipped migration. Each filename begins with a monotonic integer that is unique across the directory; the file body is engine-native SQL.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the source tree at any commit that produces a running Worker
acceptanceCriteria.when: the migrations directory is listed and each filename's leading integer is extracted
acceptanceCriteria.then: the sequence of leading integers is strictly increasing with no duplicates, every file has a non-empty SQL body, and no file in the directory falls outside the wrangler-configured pattern

acceptanceCriteria.description: Running `wrangler d1 migrations list <database> --local` against a fresh local D1 lists every file in the migrations directory as unapplied; running `wrangler d1 migrations apply <database> --local` applies them in order and a subsequent `list` reports zero unapplied.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fresh local D1 (no prior applies) and the migrations directory from AC-13102-1
acceptanceCriteria.when: the `list` then `apply` then `list` sequence runs against the local database
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first `list` prints every migration file as unapplied, the `apply` exits zero, and the second `list` prints zero unapplied migrations

acceptanceCriteria.description: The D1 bookkeeping table configured on the binding (`migrations_table`; default `d1_migrations`) holds one row per applied migration, keyed by the filename or its leading integer, after `wrangler d1 migrations apply` completes.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the local D1 after the `apply` in AC-13102-2 completes
acceptanceCriteria.when: the bookkeeping table is read via `wrangler d1 execute <database> --local --command "SELECT * FROM d1_migrations"` (or the configured `migrations_table` name)
acceptanceCriteria.then: the returned row count equals the number of migration files in the directory, and the recorded identifiers match the migration filenames or their leading integers

acceptanceCriteria.description: Quota exhausted on D1 database write. Given the D1 database is at or above the plan's per-database size ceiling (10 GB on Paid, 500 MB on Free per the vendor page) and a migration would add rows exceeding the remaining headroom, when the deploy-gate's wrangler d1 migrations apply invocation runs, then the vendor returns a quota-exhausted error, the deploy-gate exits non-zero, no migrationsApplied fires, and the wrangler deploy step is not reached (deploy is gated per REQ-003).
acceptanceCriteria.given: the D1 database is at or above the plan's size ceiling and a migration would exceed the headroom
acceptanceCriteria.when: the deploy-gate runs wrangler d1 migrations apply
acceptanceCriteria.then: the vendor returns quota exhausted; the deploy-gate exits non-zero; no migrationsApplied fires; wrangler deploy is not reached
